items.content: The light comes in sideways through tall windows, falling across tables where almost no one sits. A woman turns a page, and the sound of it carries farther than it should, soft as a breath but somehow enormous in all that stillness. The shelves stand like patient witnesses, holding their thousands of voices in careful silence, waiting. Outside, the city continues its indifferent noise, but here time has thickened into something you could almost touch.

items.content: Below, the cities sprawl like shattered constellations, their amber grids and pale arterials bleeding softly into the dark. The clouds drift beneath the wing in slow, ghostly masses, swallowing whole counties and releasing them again. Up here, suspended between the hum of engines and the indifferent stars, the world feels simultaneously vast and intimate — a secret geography only the sleepless ever see. You press your forehead against the cold oval glass and wonder, briefly, who is awake down there, and why.

items.content: Below, the cities appeared as scattered embers, as though someone had flung handfuls of gold across a vast black cloth and forgotten them there. The darkness between those clusters of light felt absolute, oceanic, belonging to a world that had no interest in being seen. She pressed her forehead against the cold oval of the window and wondered, not for the first time, how many lives were burning quietly inside all that brightness.

items.content: Happy families are all alike; every unhappy family is unhappy in its own way.
